Muscle can produce lactate during exercise, but the inability to export free glucose is due to lack of glucose 6-phosphatase, not exclusive lactate export.

question: Which diagnostic clue differentiates Cori disease from von Gierke disease?
cited_learning_objective: Glycogen Storage Diseases

options.rationale: Cori disease (debranching enzyme deficiency) causes milder hypoglycemia because gluconeogenesis remains functional, unlike von Gierke where gluconeogenesis is blocked.
Severe lactic acidosis and hyperuricemia are hallmarks of von Gierke disease, not Cori disease.
Exercise-induced myoglobinuria indicates McCardle disease (muscle phosphorylase deficiency), not Cori disease.
Cardiomyopathy in infancy is more characteristic of Pompe disease due to lysosomal accumulation, not Cori disease.
Linear insoluble glycogen and cirrhosis describe Andersen disease (branching enzyme deficiency), not Cori disease.
